history.summary: A Hindu temple at Lower Hawakhana in Tura (West Garo Hills), on the Paikan-Tura-Dalu Road (Circular Road). It is listed as a well-rated (4.5/31 ratings on one directory) religious place, and a travel listing describes it as 'the heart of the Hindu community in the Garo Hills' - a major gathering point especially during Durga Puja, set amid the lush greenery of the Tura hills. NO published history, founder, founding date, or presiding-deity information could be found - all beyond the directory facts above is UNVERIFIED. No verified photograph of this temple was found after genuine image searching (image results returned only the unrelated Thakurbari Temple of Gangtok, Sikkim), so media is empty - flagged.

name: Tura Thakurbari Temple
town_description: Tura is the largest town of the Garo Hills and the administrative headquarters of West Garo Hills district, set in a valley below Tura Peak at the western edge of Meghalaya. It is the commercial and educational hub of the Garo Hills region - a predominantly Christian town with a significant Hindu minority served by temples like the Thakurbari. Nearby attractions include Tura Peak, Pelga Falls, and Nokrek National Park (a UNESCO biosphere reserve).

travel.airport: Nearest major airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 200+ km by road; verify). Tura has a small airstrip with no scheduled commercial services (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station is the nearest major railhead (approx. 210 km by road; verify). Mendipathar (North Garo Hills) is the closest railhead within the Garo Hills (verify); onward by taxi or bus to Tura.
travel.road: The temple is in Tura town at Lower Hawakhana on the Paikan-Tura-Dalu Road (Circular Road), reachable by local transport. Tura is connected by road to Guwahati via Goalpara (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather (standard for the Garo Hills). Durga Puja (September-October) is the liveliest time.
